content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue on the latest [version_no] cloud version devices. For example, starting with a base program version v1.0, then uploading changes for v1.1 and v1.2. After cycling the power, the device reverts to the original v1.0 program. The number of used blocks does not seem to affect this behavior. Any suggestions? Solved. PM me for the solution. -[user_name]

I'm sorry, I don't fully understand your references to V1.0, V1.1, and V1.2. Are these versions of a custom program created with [product_name] software? Are they versions of a specific project file? Or do you mean something else?

Could it be that you saved program version V1.0 onto an SD card before transferring to the device? If so, this could cause the effect you're describing. Remove the SD card from the device, upload version V1.1 or V1.2, then cycle the power. After that, V1.2 should operate on the device.

No, that's not the case. The "Copy to SD card" option was not activated; transfer was only made to program memory. The program memory in the device is non-volatile and you shouldn't need to save it to the SD card. On each restart, the device first checks for a program on the SD card and loads it if present.

Just to add: I can't view your specific setup, but your issue matches what happens when the "Save to SD card" option is active during program transfer. When you upload a new program, the previous one is overwritten in program memory and should not remain in the device.
I see things differently. It's the user's responsibility: If you activate the "Copy to SD card" option, this is not [company_name]'s fault. By default, this setting is not enabled.

Where did I say or do that? How could I copy anything to the SD card when it's not even inserted? Maybe I should record a video to demonstrate, but not for you. PM me if you need instructions to resolve this. Goodbye.
I don't need instructions or a video from you. I'm well aware of how programs work on an SD card.

analysis.insight_summary: Users observed that after program updates on [product_name] device with [version_no], power cycling caused the device to revert to an older program version. This is due to the device's logic of prioritizing the SD card program over internal memory upon reboot if an SD card is present. Misunderstandings surrounding program storage options and memory management led to user frustration, indicating a need for clearer interface guidance regarding data handling and persistence.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that once a new program is uploaded to the device, it should persist even after power loss, without reverting to a previous version. They anticipate clear and intuitive memory management, ensuring newly uploaded programs remain active unless deliberately replaced.
